lead: Health products a person keeps for themselves or someone they care for, from medicines, monitors and supplements to mobility, hearing, vision and sexual-health aids. It is organised by department of need, with use classes and makers that cover the market or top independent tests.
ax: What is the product for: treating a complaint, measuring or dosing, treating an injury or supporting the body, supplying nutrients, easing breathing, sleep or pain, moving about, daily care, hearing, seeing and speaking, or family planning?
key: 1. Is it a non-prescription medicine, or a traditional or homeopathic remedy, taken or applied for a complaint? → Medicines & remedies
2. Does it read a body measure at home, test a sample, or measure out a dose (monitor, test kit, insulin pen, pill organiser)? → Monitors, tests & dosing
3. Does it dress a wound, deal with an emergency, support a joint or replace a body part? → First aid & supports
4. Is it a vitamin, herb, protein, sports fuel or medical formula? → Supplements & nutrition
5. Is it a machine, pack, lamp or bedding that eases breathing, sleep, mood or pain? → Breathing, sleep & therapy
6. Does it help someone walk, roll, cross a step or be lifted? → Mobility aids
7. Does it help with washing, the toilet, continence, bed, calling for help, reaching, dressing or eating? → Daily living & care
8. Is it a hearing aid, or a tool that brings sound and alerts to a person with hearing loss? → Hearing
9. Is it a lens, magnifier, cane or braille tool for poor sight, or an aid for speaking? → Vision & communication
10. Is it for contraception, conceiving, pregnancy, breastfeeding or intimate function? → Sexual health & family

Precedence: a tablet for sleep is a medicine (step 1) before a sleep device (step 5); a probiotic capsule is a supplement (step 4) but a probiotic yoghurt is food (J3); glasses frames and sunglasses → A4; sex toys → H3.

depts.note: Grouped by use class only; definitions name the class and active ingredient, never a health claim.
depts.t: Non-prescription products swallowed, applied, sprayed or dropped to treat a complaint, plus traditional remedies; vitamins and sports products → Supplements & nutrition; devices that read or dose → Monitors, tests & dosing.
depts.ax: What complaint is the medicine taken for: colds and allergy, pain and sleep, the gut, skin, eyes, ears and mouth, quitting smoking, or general ills treated by a healing system?

s.t: Remedies for a cold, cough, blocked nose, sore throat or hay fever; a steam device → Breathing, sleep & therapy.
s.ax: kinds by symptom, from a whole cold to the nose, chest and throat, then allergy

k.a: cold medicine · flu remedy · multi-symptom cold relief
k.d: Combination medicine for cold and flu symptoms, usually a painkiller with a decongestant and sometimes a cough or sedating ingredient.

k.a: blocked-nose spray · decongestant tablets
k.d: Medicine that relieves a blocked nose, taken as a nasal spray or by mouth.

k.a: sinus rinse · neti pot
k.d: Salt-water spray or rinse kit that flushes mucus and allergens from the nose.

k.a: chest rub · menthol rub
k.d: Menthol, camphor and eucalyptus ointment rubbed on the chest or inhaled to ease a blocked nose and cough.

k.a: cough syrup · cough mixture · cough suppressant · expectorant
k.d: Syrup, liquid or tablet taken for a cough, either to suppress a dry cough or to loosen phlegm in a chesty cough.

k.a: throat lozenge · cough drop · cough sweet · pastille · throat spray
k.d: Medicated lozenge dissolved slowly in the mouth, or spray, for a sore throat or cough.

k.a: oral antihistamine · hay-fever tablets · allergy tablets
k.d: Tablet, capsule or liquid antihistamine taken by mouth for hay fever and other allergy symptoms.

k.a: hay-fever nasal spray · steroid nasal spray
k.d: Spray used in the nose for hay fever and other allergy symptoms.

s.t: Medicines taken or rubbed on for pain, fever or poor sleep; a heat pack or TENS unit → Breathing, sleep & therapy.
s.ax: kinds by what is eased and who takes it: general pain, children, local pain, sleep

k.a: oral analgesic · pain reliever · headache tablets · migraine medicine
k.d: Tablet, capsule or liquid taken by mouth to relieve pain or bring down fever.

k.a: infant paracetamol · children's ibuprofen · infant suspension · Calpol
k.d: Paracetamol or ibuprofen in child doses, usually a flavoured oral suspension dosed by age or weight.

k.a: pain-relief gel · muscle rub · heat rub · pain patch · lidocaine patch
k.d: Gel, cream, rub or adhesive patch applied to the skin over a sore muscle or joint.

k.a: night-time sleep aid · sleeping tablets (non-prescription)
k.d: Non-prescription medicine labelled first to help fall asleep; the same ingredient labelled first for allergy is an antihistamine.

s.t: Medicines for indigestion, wind, constipation, diarrhoea, dehydration and travel sickness; a probiotic → Supplements & nutrition.
s.ax: kinds from the top of the gut to the bottom: acid, wind, bowel, fluid loss, nausea

k.a: antacid · heartburn tablets · reflux remedy · acid reducer · indigestion liquid
k.d: Non-prescription medicine that neutralises stomach acid, forms a barrier against reflux or reduces acid production.
tt: Antacid (calcium carbonate, magnesium or aluminium salts, sodium bicarbonate)

k.a: simethicone · anti-gas
k.d: Anti-foaming medicine, usually simeticone, taken for trapped wind and bloating.

k.a: constipation remedy · stool softener · fibre supplement · enema · glycerin suppository
k.d: Medicine that loosens stools or speeds bowel movement to relieve constipation, taken by mouth or given rectally.

k.a: diarrhoea remedy · loperamide · bismuth
k.d: Non-prescription medicine that slows the gut or binds irritants to stop short-term diarrhoea.

k.a: piles cream · piles treatment
k.d: Cream, ointment or suppository applied to soothe haemorrhoids, often with a local anaesthetic or barrier base.

k.a: ORS · rehydration sachets · electrolyte solution · oral electrolyte
k.d: Measured mix of glucose and salts, as powder sachets or ready-to-drink liquid, to replace fluid lost through diarrhoea or vomiting.

k.a: motion-sickness tablets · seasickness remedy · travel sickness patch
k.d: Medicine taken before a journey to prevent nausea and vomiting from motion; usually an antihistamine or hyoscine.

s.t: Creams, drops and treatments put on the skin or into the eyes, ears and mouth; contact-lens drops → Vision & communication.
s.ax: kinds by body part: skin, feet, hair, eyes, ears, gums

k.a: antiseptic cream · antiseptic liquid · wound wash · first-aid antiseptic
k.d: Cream, liquid, spray or wipe that kills germs on minor cuts, grazes and burns.

k.a: hydrocortisone cream · anti-itch cream · bite and sting cream · calamine lotion
k.d: Cream, ointment or lotion that calms itching and inflammation from eczema, rashes, bites and stings.

k.a: athlete's foot cream · nail fungus treatment · thrush treatment · clotrimazole cream
k.d: Cream, spray, powder, nail lacquer or pessary that treats fungal infections of skin, nails or the vagina.

k.a: cold-sore cream · herpes labialis treatment · cold-sore patch
k.d: Antiviral cream, docosanol cream or hydrocolloid patch applied at the first tingle of a cold sore.

k.a: corn plaster · callus remover · wart remover · verruca gel · freeze spray
k.d: Medicated plaster, gel, liquid or freeze spray for removing corns, calluses, warts and verrucas at home.

k.a: nit treatment · lice lotion · lice comb · nit comb
k.d: Lotion, spray or fine-toothed comb used to kill or remove head lice and their eggs.

k.a: artificial tears · lubricating eye drops · allergy eye drops · red-eye drops
k.d: Liquid or gel drops put into the eye to relieve dryness, irritation, redness or allergy; contact-lens drops sit under Vision.

k.a: earwax drops · ear-wax remover · swimmer's ear drops
k.d: Drops put into the ear canal to soften wax, dry the canal after swimming or ease outer-ear soreness.

k.a: teething gel · gum gel · teething relief
k.d: Gel rubbed onto a baby's gums to soothe teething pain; local-anaesthetic and salicylate gels are age-restricted in some markets.
tt: Benzocaine (not for under-2s in the US)
Choline salicylate (not for under-16s in the UK)

s.t: Products that supply nicotine without tobacco smoke to help a person stop; an ordinary vape → J10.

k.a: nicotine replacement product · NRT · stop-smoking aid
k.d: Product that supplies a measured dose of nicotine without tobacco smoke, used to help stop smoking.
see: nicotine product that is not a quit aid

s.t: Preparations sold under a healing system rather than for one complaint; a herb sold as a supplement → Supplements & nutrition.
s.ax: kinds by healing system: homeopathy, then other traditional systems

k.a: homeopathic remedy · mono-preparation · single remedy
k.d: Registered homeopathic preparation of one starting substance, sold as pills or liquid at a stated dilution; no efficacy claims made here.

k.a: traditional remedy · herbal medicine · patent medicine · Kampo extract · Ayurvedic medicine · Unani medicine
k.d: Ready-made preparation from a traditional healing system such as Chinese, Kampo, Ayurvedic, Unani or Western herbal medicine; no efficacy claims made here.

depts.note: Validated accuracy is the first test for every monitor.
depts.t: Devices that read a body measure, test a sample at home or measure out a dose; pregnancy and ovulation tests → Sexual health & family; a fitness watch → D2.
depts.ax: What does the device do: read a body measure again and again, track glucose, test a sample once, or measure out a dose?

s.t: Home monitors for blood pressure, temperature, blood oxygen, heart rhythm and breathing; a stethoscope-only kit is a manual kit here.
s.ax: kinds by what is measured: blood pressure, temperature, oxygen, heart rhythm, breath flow

k.a: home BP monitor · digital sphygmomanometer · BP cuff
k.d: Automatic home monitor that inflates a cuff and shows systolic, diastolic pressure and pulse; choose one on a validation list.

k.a: aneroid sphygmomanometer · manual BP cuff
k.d: Gauge with arm cuff and hand bulb, read by listening with a stethoscope; sold with or without the stethoscope.

k.a: electronic thermometer · fever thermometer · ear thermometer · forehead thermometer
k.d: Electronic thermometer for checking body temperature, read in the mouth, under the arm, in the ear or on the forehead.
see: workshop tool, not for the body

k.a: finger oximeter · SpO2 monitor
k.d: Small clip-on or worn sensor that reads blood oxygen saturation and pulse rate.

k.a: home ECG · portable EKG
k.d: Handheld or worn device that records a short electrocardiogram at home to check heart rhythm.

k.a: PEF meter · asthma peak flow meter
k.d: Handheld tube with a scale that measures how fast a person can breathe out, used to monitor asthma.

s.t: Meters and sensors that follow blood sugar; an insulin pen or pump → Dosing devices.
s.ax: kinds from continuous sensor to single reading to long-term average

k.a: CGM · flash glucose monitor · glucose sensor
k.d: Worn sensor that measures glucose under the skin and sends readings to a phone, reader or pump at short intervals.

k.a: glucometer · fingerstick meter
k.d: Handheld meter that reads a drop of fingerstick blood on a one-use test strip.

k.a: HbA1c home test kit · A1C test
k.d: One-use kit that measures average blood glucose (HbA1c) from a fingerstick blood sample.

s.t: One-use kits that test a sample at home for infection, markers or alcohol; a pregnancy test → Sexual health & family.
s.ax: kinds by what is tested: infection, urine, blood, stool, breath

k.a: at-home infection test · rapid antigen self-test · lateral flow test
k.d: Self-test kit for a respiratory or other infection, such as COVID-19 or flu; a combined test counts as one product.

k.a: urine dipstick · urinalysis strips · UTI test
k.d: Paper strips with reagent pads dipped in urine to show infection markers or other values by colour change.

k.a: home HIV test · HIV home test kit
k.d: Over-the-counter rapid test that detects HIV antibodies from an oral swab or a drop of fingerstick blood.

k.a: home cholesterol test · lipid test kit · cholesterol meter
k.d: Fingerstick test or small meter that measures blood cholesterol at home.

k.a: faecal immunochemical test · FIT · home bowel cancer test · stool test
k.d: Home stool-sample kit that checks for hidden blood, a possible sign of bowel cancer, and is posted to a laboratory.

k.a: breathalyzer · personal breathalyser · alcohol tester · alcohol meter
k.d: Handheld device that estimates blood alcohol from a breath sample, for checking you are fit to drive.

s.t: Devices that deliver or measure out a dose of medicine; the medicine itself → Medicines & remedies.
s.ax: kinds from injected doses to oral doses to organising tablets

k.a: injector pen · insulin injection pen
k.d: Pen-shaped injector that delivers a dialled dose of insulin through a single-use pen needle.

k.a: CSII pump · automated insulin delivery (AID) system
k.d: Small worn pump that delivers rapid-acting insulin continuously under the skin, often adjusted automatically from a CGM.

k.a: epinephrine autoinjector · adrenaline pen · AAI · EpiPen
k.d: A prescribed single-use pen with a fixed dose of adrenaline and a spring-loaded needle, carried for emergency treatment of anaphylaxis.

k.a: medicine measure · dosing cup
k.d: Needleless syringe, spoon or cup that measures a dose of liquid medicine.

k.a: pillbox · pill box · dosette box · pill case · medication dispenser · pill reminder
k.d: A compartmented box or alarmed device that holds scheduled doses of tablets so the user takes the right dose at the right time.
tt: Connected smart dispenser with app alerts

k.a: pill splitter · pill crusher
k.d: Small blade holder that cuts a tablet in two; some models also crush it.

ms.note: worldwide share by monetary value in FY2015, Omron's own research; the global market was 40 million units

depts.msum: Omron states it held about 46 % of the world home blood-pressure monitor market by value in 2015. No independent ranking was found.

depts.note: Medical face masks arrive here from clothing.
depts.t: Items that treat an injury, hold a joint or replace a missing body part; a medicine for the wound → Medicines & remedies; sports kit that is not medical → E2.
depts.ax: What does the item do for the body: cover a wound, deal with an emergency, support a joint or limb, or replace a missing part?

s.t: Kits, plasters, dressings and bandages for cuts, grazes and burns; a medicated antiseptic → Medicines & remedies.
s.ax: kinds from the whole kit to single dressings, then what holds them

k.a: Verbandkasten · first-aid box · grab bag
k.d: Boxed or bagged set of dressings and basics sold as one product; compare by the standard and size class it meets.

k.a: adhesive bandage · sticking plaster · Band-Aid · Elastoplast
k.d: Small dressing pad on an adhesive strip for minor cuts; blister plasters use a hydrocolloid gel cushion.
see: builder's wall plaster, a different object with the same name

k.a: gauze pad · non-stick pad
k.d: Sterile pad laid over a wound and held with tape or a bandage; larger than a plaster.

k.a: burn gel pad · hydrogel dressing
k.d: Cooling gel dressing that covers a minor burn or scald.

k.a: roller bandage · gauze bandage · triangular bandage · sling · tubular bandage
k.d: Strip, tube or triangle of fabric used to hold a dressing, support a limb or make a sling.

k.a: surgical tape · micropore tape
k.d: Roll of adhesive tape that holds a dressing or bandage in place.

k.a: Steri-Strip · butterfly closure · butterfly stitch
k.d: Thin porous adhesive strips that pull the edges of a small cut together while it heals.

k.a: spray plaster · liquid plaster
k.d: Liquid or spray that dries to a thin protective polymer film over a minor wound.

s.t: Kept for an emergency or to protect the helper; a worker's respirator → C1.
s.ax: kinds by emergency: heart stop, exposure, eye splash, infection risk

k.a: home AED · automated external defibrillator · public-access defibrillator
k.d: Automated external defibrillator kept at home or in a community cabinet that analyses heart rhythm and guides the rescuer with voice prompts.

k.a: space blanket · rescue blanket
k.d: Thin heat-reflecting sheet that stops body heat loss after an accident or exposure.

k.a: eye wash · eye bath
k.d: Sterile saline in a bottle, pod or wall station that rinses the eye after dust or a splash.

k.a: examination gloves · nitrile gloves
k.d: One-use gloves worn when treating wounds or cleaning up, to limit cross-contamination.

k.a: surgical face mask
k.d: Mask worn over the nose and mouth for medical or surgical protection.
see: protective mask for dust and fumes

s.t: Worn supports that steady a joint or limb, shape the foot or squeeze the leg; a sports-brand brace is the same kind.
s.ax: kinds by what the support does: hold a joint, hold a limb, shape the foot, squeeze the leg

k.a: knee brace · ankle brace · back brace · wrist splint · elbow strap · cervical collar · lumbar support
k.d: Elastic, strapped or hinged support worn to steady or protect a joint or the spine; body part is the main variant.

k.a: arm sling · finger splint
k.d: Support that keeps an injured arm, hand or finger still while it heals.

k.a: orthotics · arch-support insole · foot orthosis
k.d: Shoe insert that supports the arch or redistributes pressure to treat or prevent foot pain.
tt: Custom-made from a cast or scan
see: comfort insole sold with shoe care

k.a: compression socks · support stockings · graduated compression hosiery
k.d: Stocking with graduated pressure, strongest at the ankle, for leg veins, swelling or travel.

s.t: Artificial limbs and body parts fitted by a specialist; an implant is surgery, not a possession.
s.ax: kinds by body part replaced: leg, arm, breast, eye, face

k.a: artificial leg · lower-limb prosthesis
k.d: Artificial leg or part of one, built from a socket, knee, pylon and foot, fitted by a prosthetist.

k.a: artificial arm · upper-limb prosthesis · bionic hand
k.d: Artificial arm, hand or part of one, either body-powered or electrically driven.

k.a: breast form · mastectomy prosthesis
k.d: External artificial breast worn in a bra after mastectomy or for asymmetry; also breast forms and packers.

k.a: artificial eye · ocular prosthesis
k.d: Artificial eye, usually custom-made in acrylic and painted to match the other eye.

k.a: epithesis
k.d: Custom prosthesis replacing a facial or other external part such as an ear or nose.

depts.t: Capsules, powders, drinks and formulas taken to add nutrients or fuel training or diet; a medicine → Medicines & remedies; a food or ready drink → J.
depts.ax: What does it supply: vitamins and minerals, oils, herbs and specialty ingredients, training protein, endurance fuel, or whole-diet nutrition?

s.t: Supplements built on vitamins, minerals or both together.

k.a: multi · multivitamin and mineral · A–Z multi
k.d: Supplement that combines many vitamins, usually with minerals, in one daily dose.

k.a: single vitamin · vitamin D · vitamin C · B12 · B complex · folic acid
k.d: Supplement built around one vitamin or one vitamin group, such as D, C or the B complex.

k.a: single mineral · magnesium · iron · zinc · calcium
k.d: Supplement built around one mineral, such as magnesium, iron, zinc or calcium.

s.t: Supplements built on an oil, microbe, plant or protein rather than a vitamin or mineral.
s.ax: kinds from oils and microbes to herbs, collagen and blends

k.a: fish oil · omega-3 · EPA/DHA supplement
k.d: Oil supplement supplying the omega-3 fats EPA and DHA, in softgels, liquid or gummies.

k.a: probiotic supplement · live cultures
k.d: Supplement of live microbes such as Lactobacillus, Bifidobacterium or Saccharomyces strains, in capsules, powders or gummies.

k.a: herbal remedy · botanical supplement · ashwagandha supplement
k.d: Supplement made from a single plant's root, leaf or extract, sold as capsules, powder, tea or tincture.

k.a: collagen supplement · collagen peptides · hydrolysed collagen
k.d: Collagen protein, usually hydrolysed into peptides, sold as powder, drink, gummy or capsule.

k.a: multi-ingredient supplement · joint formula · hair, skin and nails formula
k.d: Product mixing several ingredient classes, such as a joint formula or a hair, skin and nails formula.

k.a: essence of chicken · chicken essence · restorative essence
k.d: Bottled tonic or essence, such as chicken essence, taken as a supplement, mainly in East and South-East Asia.

s.t: Powders and capsules taken around training for muscle, energy or weight; a protein bar → J8.
s.ax: kinds from bulk protein to focused ingredients, then stimulants and fat loss

k.a: whey · whey protein · casein · protein shake powder · vegan protein
k.d: Powder sold mainly for its protein, mixed into shakes for training, recovery or diet.

k.a: weight gainer · gainer
k.d: High-calorie protein and carbohydrate powder for gaining weight.

k.a: creatine monohydrate · Creapure
k.d: Creatine, usually monohydrate, sold as a training supplement.

k.a: BCAA · EAA · glutamine · intra-workout
k.d: Amino acids such as BCAAs, EAAs or glutamine sold for training.

k.a: pre · pre-workout powder
k.d: Powder or drink taken before training, usually with caffeine and pump or endurance ingredients.

k.a: thermogenic · weight-loss supplement
k.d: Supplement, often caffeine-based, sold to accompany a diet and training for weight loss.

s.t: Carbohydrate and salt products taken during long exercise; a ready-made sports drink → J9.

k.a: energy gel · sports gel · endurance gel · carbohydrate gel · energy chew · energy blok
k.d: Single-serve carbohydrate gel or chewable sweet taken during endurance exercise to keep up energy.

k.a: hydration drink mix · electrolyte powder · hydration tablets · electrolyte tabs · sports drink powder
k.d: Powder, sachet or effervescent tablet mixed into water to replace fluid, salts and sometimes carbohydrate during or after exercise.

s.t: Products that stand in for a meal or feed a medical condition, from diet shakes to clinical formulas.
s.ax: kinds from diet shake to nutrition drink to condition-specific formula

k.a: meal shake · complete food · drinkable meal · meal-replacement powder · diet shake
k.d: Powder or ready-to-drink shake made to replace a whole meal with set calories and nutrients.

k.a: ONS · sip feed · nutritional drink · supplement drink · complete nutrition drink
k.d: Energy- and nutrient-dense drink or powder taken alongside food when appetite or diet falls short, often under medical advice.

k.a: hypoallergenic formula · amino-acid formula · elemental formula · metabolic formula · food for special medical purposes · medical food
k.d: Formula made for the dietary management of a medical condition, such as allergy or a metabolic disorder; a food, not a supplement.

ms.note: Haleon states it is the largest player; its own analysis of third-party data

depts.msum: Haleon states it is the largest vitamins, minerals and supplements company in 2023, with about 3 % of the world market, so the field is fragmented.

depts.t: Machines, packs, lamps and bedding that ease breathing, sleep, mood or pain; a medicine for the same complaint → Medicines & remedies; a massager → H1.
depts.ax: What does the device ease: breathing, sleep and mood, or pain and comfort?

s.t: Machines and holders that help air or inhaled medicine reach the lungs, by day or in sleep.
s.ax: kinds from machines that supply air to those that deliver medicine or steam

k.a: CPAP · APAP · auto-CPAP · sleep apnoea machine · PAP machine
k.d: Bedside pump that blows pressurised air through a hose and mask to keep the airway open during sleep.

k.a: oxygen machine · POC · portable oxygen concentrator · home oxygen concentrator
k.d: Machine that filters nitrogen from room air to deliver oxygen-rich air through a cannula or mask.

k.a: nebulizer · inhalation device
k.d: Device that turns liquid medicine into a mist to be breathed in.

k.a: spacer · valved holding chamber · VHC · aerochamber
k.d: Chamber fitted between a metered-dose inhaler and the mouth so the dose can be breathed in slowly.

k.a: personal steam inhaler · steam vaporiser · facial steamer
k.d: Device that makes warm steam to be breathed in for cold, cough or sinus relief, without liquid medicine.

s.t: Devices and bedding that improve sleep or lift winter mood; a sleeping tablet → Medicines & remedies.

k.a: snoring mouthpiece · mandibular advancement device · MAD · anti-snore mouth guard
k.d: Night-time aid, usually a mouthpiece that holds the lower jaw forward, to reduce snoring.

k.a: gravity blanket · sensory blanket
k.d: Heavy blanket filled with beads or pellets, giving even pressure to calm and aid sleep.

k.a: SAD lamp · light box · daylight lamp · energy light
k.d: Bright lamp, typically 10,000 lux at a set distance, used daily to lift winter mood or reset sleep timing.
see: bedside lamp sold for the home

s.t: Devices that ease sore muscles, joints and the neck through current, heat, cold or support.

k.a: TENS unit · EMS unit · TENS machine · muscle stimulator
k.d: Battery pulse unit with skin pads that stimulates nerves (TENS) to ease pain or muscles (EMS) to contract them.

k.a: heat patch · heat wrap · heating pad · ice pack · cold pack · hot-water bottle
k.d: Pack, patch or pad applied to the body to warm or cool a sore muscle, joint or injury.

k.a: cervical pillow · contour pillow · neck pillow
k.d: Shaped or adjustable pillow made to support the neck, back or joints and ease pain in bed.

depts.note: Archetypes only for active wheelchairs and collector canes; the rest is tier.
depts.t: Aids for walking, rolling, crossing a step or being lifted; a bathroom or bed aid → Daily living & care; a hiking pole → E2.
depts.ax: How does the person move: on foot with support, seated on wheels, or lifted and carried over a step or into a vehicle?

s.t: Sticks, crutches and frames that take weight on foot; a cane owned as a collectable → Collector canes.
s.ax: kinds by how much weight they take, from a stick to a wheeled frame

k.a: cane · walking cane · assistive cane

pole for hiking, not a medical aid

Shooting stick, alpenstock, pike staff and scout staff are left out as tools, and the cane gun, canne de combat and pace stick are only cross-references there. No whole-space reference exists.
k.xg: by what the stick is known for

s.t: Chairs and scooters on wheels, pushed, self-driven or powered, with the add-ons and parts owners swap.
s.ax: kinds by what moves it: user or helper, motor, add-on drive, then parts

k.a: self-propelled wheelchair · transit chair · attendant-propelled chair · companion chair
k.d: Wheelchair moved by the user pushing the rims or by a helper pushing from behind.

x.d: First lightweight, steel, folding, portable wheelchair; the first mass-market wheelchair.
Lightweight, adjustable aluminium-frame chair launched as a custom active-user wheelchair.
x.dt: co-founded by Marilyn Hamilton, Jim Okamoto and Don Helman · aluminium frame · colour options

x.d: Ultralight competition chair designed by Rainer Küschall, about 14 kg against the usual 25 kg.
x.dt: MoMA collection, first medical device in it · rigid frame

x.d: Custom ultralight rigid-frame chair, built in titanium, aluminium or carbon fibre and fitted per user.
x.dt: titanium, aluminium or carbon-fibre frame · TiFit measured build

k.nl: One entry is a manual wheelchair line that a fetched page names as a milestone in the chair's history; models and sizes are not entries.
k.sel: No whole-space reference exists. The four lines are those with their own Wikipedia articles or sections (Wheelchair, Marilyn Hamilton, Rainer Küschall, TiLite); the Everest & Jennings chair is the first mass-market wheelchair on the Wheelchair page.

k.a: power chair · powerchair · electric wheelchair · motorised wheelchair
k.d: Wheelchair driven by battery and electric motors, steered with a joystick or other control.

k.a: electric scooter · buggy · gopher
k.d: Electric seated vehicle with tiller steering made for a person with limited mobility.

k.a: power assist · power-assist wheels · e-handbike attachment · wheelchair power pack
k.d: Battery drive fitted to a manual wheelchair to add motor help while keeping the chair.

k.a: wheelchair part · wheelchair accessory · wheelchair cushion
k.d: Replacement part or add-on for a wheelchair or scooter, including seat cushions, wheels and controls.

s.t: Aids that change a person's height or position: over a step, between seats, or into a vehicle.
s.ax: kinds by the move they make: roll over a step, lift, slide or pivot, load into a vehicle

k.a: wheelchair ramp · threshold ramp · suitcase ramp
k.d: Movable ramp that lets a wheelchair or scooter cross steps, kerbs or door thresholds.

k.a: hoist · Hoyer lift · sling lift · stand aid
k.d: Powered or hydraulic hoist that lifts a person in a sling or standing frame between bed, chair and toilet.

k.a: transfer board · sliding board · turntable · pivot disc · standing aid
k.d: Non-powered aid that helps a person slide, pivot or stand to move between bed, chair, car and wheelchair.

k.a: scooter lift · boot hoist · hitch lift
k.d: Powered lift fitted inside a car or on its hitch that raises a mobility scooter or wheelchair into or onto the vehicle.

depts.t: Aids that help a person wash, use the toilet, stay continent, rest in bed, call for help or manage meals and dressing; built-in grab bars and stairlifts → G3.
depts.ax: Which part of daily life does the aid help with: washing and toileting, continence, rest in bed, calling for help, or reaching, dressing and eating?

s.t: Seats, frames and tools for washing and using the toilet safely.
s.ax: kinds from bathing to toileting: bath, shower, toilet, commode

k.a: shower stool · shower seat · bath seat
k.d: Chair, stool or seat for sitting safely while washing.

k.a: bath transfer bench
k.d: Bench that straddles the bath wall so a person sits outside and slides across into the bath.

k.a: bath lifter · bathing cushion
k.d: Powered seat that lowers a person into the bath and raises them out again.
see: bench that slides a person into the bath

k.a: long-handled sponge · bottom wiper
k.d: Long-handled sponge, brush or wiper that lets a person with limited reach wash and toilet alone.

k.a: toilet seat raiser
k.d: Seat fitted on a toilet bowl to raise its height so sitting and standing are easier.

k.a: toilet frame · toilet surround
k.d: Frame with armrests around a toilet that helps a person sit down and rise.
see: fixed rail built into a bathroom

k.a: commode · shower commode
k.d: Chair with a seat opening and removable pail used as a toilet, including wheeled types for the shower.

k.a: commode pan · urine bottle
k.d: Bed-side receptacle for passing urine or stools without leaving bed.

s.t: Products that contain or collect urine and stool.
s.ax: kinds from absorbent products to collecting devices to catheters

k.a: continence pads · adult nappies · adult diapers · protective underwear · incontinence briefs
k.d: Disposable or washable absorbent product worn to contain urinary or bowel leakage.

k.a: underpad · bed pad · chair pad
k.d: Absorbent pad laid on a bed or seat to protect it from leaks.

k.a: ostomy bag · stoma bag · ostomy pouching system
k.d: Pouch and skin barrier worn over a stoma to collect output.

k.a: self-catheter · ISC catheter
k.d: Single-use tube a person passes into the bladder to drain urine, then removes.

k.a: condom catheter · male external catheter
k.d: Sheath worn on the penis that carries urine to a drainage bag, with no tube inside the body.

k.a: leg bag · catheter bag
k.d: Bag strapped to the leg or hung from the bed that collects urine from a catheter.

s.t: Beds, mattresses, cushions and rails for someone who spends long hours lying or sitting.
s.ax: kinds from the bed to what lies on it, sits on it or guards its edge

k.a: hospital bed · nursing bed · profiling bed · home-care bed
k.d: Height-adjustable bed with a profiling mattress platform, used for nursing care at home.

k.a: pressure-care mattress · anti-decubitus mattress · alternating-pressure mattress
k.d: Mattress or overlay that spreads or shifts body pressure to prevent or treat pressure sores.

k.a: pressure-care cushion · wheelchair cushion · seat cushion
k.d: Seat cushion, including wheelchair cushions, that spreads or shifts pressure to prevent or treat pressure sores.

k.a: bed guard · side rail · cot side · bed assist handle
k.d: Rail or handle fitted to a bed to prevent falls or help a person sit up and stand.

k.a: riser recliner · rise and recline chair
k.d: Powered armchair that tilts the whole seat forward to help the user stand, often with a recline.

s.t: Worn or fitted items that call help or tell others about a condition.

k.a: care alarm · pendant alarm · telecare alarm · fall alarm · medical alert system
k.d: Worn call button or sensor that summons help after a fall or medical event, often through a monitoring service.
see: alarm for personal safety, not medical

k.a: medical alert bracelet · medic alert tag · SOS bracelet · ICE ID
k.d: Worn or carried item engraved or printed with medical conditions and emergency contacts.

k.a: wander alarm · door exit alarm · dementia door alarm
k.d: Device that alerts carers when a person at risk leaves a room, bed or home.

s.t: Hand tools and adapted tableware for reaching, dressing, eating and gripping.
s.ax: kinds by task: reach, dress, eat, grip

k.a: grabber · pick-up tool · helping hand · reach extender · litter picker
k.d: Hand-held pole with a trigger-operated jaw for picking things up from the floor or high shelves without bending or stretching.

k.a: sock aid · stocking aid · button hook · dressing stick · long shoehorn
k.d: Simple tool that helps a person with limited bending, reach or grip put on socks, shoes and fastenings.

k.a: adaptive eating utensils · easy-grip cutlery · assistive eating devices · tremor spoon
k.d: Cutlery, plates and cups shaped, weighted or stabilised so people with weak grip or tremor can eat and drink unaided.

k.a: tap turner · jar opener
k.d: Tool that gives grip or leverage to open jars, bottles and taps for people with weak hands.

depts.t: Devices for people with hearing loss: aids worn in or on the ear, their care and parts, and tools that bring sound and alerts to the listener; earplugs and headphones → C1, D3.
depts.ax: Where does the device work: worn at the ear, caring for the ear device, or carrying sound and alerts to the listener?

s.t: Devices worn in or on the ear to amplify sound or drive an implant.
s.ax: kinds from prescribed aids to over-the-counter aids to amplifiers and implant processors

k.a: RIC hearing aid · RITE · BTE · ITE · ITC · CIC · IIC · miniRITE
k.d: Prescription device worn in or behind the ear that amplifies sound for a person with hearing loss; form factor varies.

k.a: OTC hearing aid · self-fitting hearing aid
k.d: Hearing aid sold without a prescription for adults with perceived mild to moderate loss, fitted and adjusted by the user.

k.a: PSAP · personal sound amplification product · hearing amplifier
k.d: Wearable electronic sound amplifier for people without hearing loss; not regulated or sold as a hearing aid.

k.a: cochlear implant processor · bone-conduction processor · audio processor
k.d: External processor worn on the head that picks up sound and drives a cochlear or bone-anchored hearing implant.

s.t: Batteries and small parts that keep a hearing aid running.

k.a: hearing-aid battery · dome · ear tip · wax guard
k.d: Consumables and small parts for a hearing aid: batteries, domes and tips, wax guards and tubes.

s.t: Tools that carry speech, TV sound and alarms to a person with hearing loss.
s.ax: kinds by what they carry: remote voice, TV or room sound, phone calls, alarms

k.a: TV streamer · TV connector · partner mic · remote microphone · hearing-aid remote control
k.d: Wireless accessory from a hearing-aid maker that streams TV or a speaker's voice to the aids, or adjusts them remotely.

k.a: hearing loop · TV listener
k.d: Transmitter and receiver that carry sound from a TV, speaker or room straight to a listener or their hearing aid.

k.a: big-button phone · hearing phone
k.d: Telephone with extra volume and tone control for people with hearing loss.

k.a: deaf alerting system · visual alert · bed shaker · vibrating alarm clock · doorbell flasher · signaller
k.d: Transmitters and receivers that turn alarm clocks, doorbells, phones and smoke alarms into flashes or vibrations for people with hearing loss.
see: ordinary alarm the transmitter listens to

depts.msum: Six makers shared the hearing-aid market in 2012: Sonova 24 %, Demant 23 %, Sivantos 17 %, GN 16 %, Starkey and Widex 9 % each. The figures are by units and are old; WS Audiology formed in 2019 from Sivantos and Widex.

depts.note: Frames, ready readers and all glasses move to A4 Eyewear; lenses, contacts and low-vision aids stay here.
depts.t: Lenses and aids for people who see poorly or cannot see, and aids for people who cannot rely on speech; frames and sunglasses → A4; a hobby loupe → E6.
depts.ax: What does the person need help with: seeing through corrected lenses, using limited sight, getting around and reading without sight, or speaking?

s.t: Prescription lenses worn in glasses or on the eye, and their care.
s.ax: kinds from lenses in glasses to lenses on the eye to their care

k.a: prescription lens · glasses lens · varifocal lens
k.d: Prescription lens glazed into a spectacle frame, from single vision to progressive, with optional coatings and tints.
see: the frames the lenses are glazed into

k.a: contacts · disposable lens
k.d: Flexible lens worn on the eye, of any replacement schedule, correction or colour; plano coloured lenses included.

k.a: RGP lens · gas-permeable lens · GP lens · hard lens · ortho-k · scleral lens
k.d: Rigid gas-permeable lens worn by day, overnight to reshape the cornea, or as a large scleral lens vaulting the cornea.

k.a: contact solution · lens care · rewetting drops
k.d: Solutions for cleaning, disinfecting, rinsing and storing contact lenses, and drops to rewet lenses in the eye.

s.t: Magnifiers and optical aids that make the most of remaining sight.
s.ax: kinds from simple magnifiers to electronic and worn aids

k.a: hand magnifier · magnifying glass · pocket magnifier
k.d: Magnifier held in the hand, made and sold as a low-vision aid.
see: the same tool sold for hobby use

k.a: illuminated stand magnifier · bright-field magnifier
k.d: Magnifier on a stand or flat base resting on the page, made and sold as a low-vision aid.
see: the same tool sold for hobby use

k.a: video magnifier · CCTV · digital magnifier
k.d: Camera-and-screen device that enlarges print and images for a low-vision user.

k.a: low-vision spectacles · spectacle magnifier · bioptic telescope
k.d: Spectacles with magnifying, prismatic or telescopic lenses, including clip-on and flip-down telescopes.

k.a: low-vision telescope · handheld telescope
k.d: Small handheld telescope made and sold as a low-vision aid for seeing at a distance.

s.t: Canes and braille tools used without sight.

k.a: long cane · mobility cane · symbol cane
k.d: Cane made for a blind or low-vision person to detect obstacles or show that they cannot see well.

k.a: braille writer · braille display · braille note-taker
k.d: Device for writing or reading braille: a mechanical braille writer, a refreshable pin display or a braille note-taker.

x.d: Six-key mechanical braille typewriter designed by David Abraham, the standard braille writer for decades.

v.n: Light Touch, Unimanual and large-cell versions
v.d: for low hand strength, one hand, jumbo cells

x.dt: standard or large cell · light-touch or one-hand keys

k.nl: One entry is a braille writing or reading device line sold under its own name; later and adapted versions are versions.
k.sel: No whole-space reference exists. The one entry is the Perkins Brailler, which has its own Wikipedia article; makers of braille displays and note-takers are in the brand register.

s.t: Devices and boards that let a person speak or be understood without ordinary speech.

k.a: AAC device · speech-generating device · voice output communication aid
k.d: Device or board that speaks or shows messages for a person who cannot rely on their own speech.

k.a: eye tracker · eye-gaze communication device
k.d: Eye tracker fixed to a computer or tablet so a person with little movement can control it and communicate by gaze.

k.a: artificial larynx · speech aid
k.d: Battery device held to the throat that makes a voice for people who have lost their voice box.

depts.t: Products for preventing or planning pregnancy, feeding a baby and intimate function; sex toys → H3; period products → H1.
depts.ax: What stage or need is it for: contraception and barriers, conceiving and confirming pregnancy, breastfeeding, or intimate function?

s.t: Products that prevent pregnancy or infection during sex.
s.ax: kinds from the worn barrier to fitted barriers to chemical and emergency methods

k.a: rubber · sheath · external condom · internal condom · female condom
k.d: Thin sheath worn on the penis or inside the vagina as a contraceptive and barrier against infection.

k.a: oral dam
k.d: Thin latex or polyurethane sheet placed over the genitals or anus as a barrier during oral sex.

k.a: cervical barrier
k.d: Reusable cup fitted over the cervix with spermicide as a barrier contraceptive.

k.a: contraceptive gel · contraceptive film
k.d: Gel, film or foam placed in the vagina before sex to kill sperm.

k.a: morning-after pill · emergency contraception
k.d: Single-dose pill taken soon after unprotected sex to lower the chance of pregnancy.

s.t: Tests and trackers for trying to conceive and for confirming pregnancy.
s.ax: kinds from tracking the cycle to testing to confirming pregnancy

k.a: BBT thermometer · basal thermometer
k.d: Sensitive thermometer made to track resting body temperature on waking for fertility awareness.

k.a: hormone monitor · fertility tracker
k.d: Reusable reader with test sticks, wands or sensors that tracks hormones or temperature to show the fertile window.

k.a: ovulation predictor kit · OPK · LH test
k.d: One-use urine test that finds the hormone surge before ovulation, or confirms ovulation afterwards.

k.a: home sperm test · male fertility test · semen test
k.d: Home test that checks a semen sample for sperm concentration or motile sperm, for fertility or after vasectomy.

k.a: home pregnancy test · hCG test
k.d: One-use urine test that detects the pregnancy hormone hCG to show whether the user is pregnant.

s.t: Pumps and care items for breastfeeding and expressing milk.
s.ax: kinds from expressing and storing milk to feeding and skin care

k.a: milk pump · wearable pump · hands-free pump
k.d: Device that draws milk from the breast by hand or motor, for feeding later.

k.a: milk catcher · breast shell
k.d: Cup worn in the bra that catches milk leaking from the other breast, without suction.

k.a: milk bag · freezer bag
k.d: Sterile freezable bag for storing expressed milk.

k.a: breastfeeding shield
k.d: Thin silicone cover worn over the nipple during a feed.

k.a: breast pad · bra liner
k.d: Pad worn inside the bra to absorb leaking milk.

k.a: nipple balm · lanolin cream
k.d: Cream or balm that soothes sore or cracked nipples during breastfeeding.

s.t: Medical devices for pelvic and sexual function; a pleasure toy → H3.
s.ax: kinds by body part: pelvic floor, vagina, penis

k.a: Kegel trainer · pelvic-floor exerciser
k.d: Device that guides or stimulates pelvic-floor muscle exercise, sold for continence or postnatal recovery.

k.a: Vaginal trainer
k.d: Smooth cylinder, usually sold as a graduated set, used to widen or restore vaginal capacity after surgery, radiotherapy or for vaginismus.

k.a: Penis pump (medical) · VED
k.d: Cylinder and pump that draws blood into the penis to produce an erection, sold to treat erectile dysfunction.

k.a: ED ring · constriction ring · tension ring
k.d: Elastic ring worn at the base of the penis to keep an erection, often used with a vacuum erection device.

k.a: Penile extender (medical)
k.d: Device worn to apply steady stretch to the penis, sold for Peyronie's disease or to preserve length after surgery.

k.a: desensitising spray
k.d: Topical anaesthetic spray applied to the penis to reduce sensitivity and delay ejaculation.
